This is why we need universal subsidized access to naloxone. One prefilled injector of naloxone in the hands of anyone who can read the box would save these people. If you have friends who use heroin (and other opioids like oxycodone, hydrocodone, methadone, etc) get your hands on a dose of naloxone to have in emergencies. If you live in the 12 states that sell it over the counter, you can get one at CVS. Otherwise ask your doctor about it. Some are going to be dicks, but many like me would love to give you an rx. Arkansas, California, Minnesota, Mississippi, Montana, New Jersey, North Dakota, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Utah, and Wisconsin are those states where it is available without a prescription.

However, if you ever are in a situation where you see a heroin overdose you don't actually need naloxone to save them, you just need a strong stomach. Heroin kills by causing respiratory depression. You become so sedated that you cease to breathe. Breathing is a mechanical function that almost anyone can do for an unconscious person until help arrives. However the 5-10+ minutes from calling EMS to arrival will kill almost anyone in respiratory arrest. If this happens do the following:

1) Call for help. If you have a phone, call 911. If not, scream at the top of your lungs for someone. If there is a crowd, pick one person out and tell them specifically to call 911. If you ask a crowd sometimes no one will do it thinking everyone else will.

2) Place the person on their back and tilt their head a bit back (like they were looking up above their head) so their nose is pointing straight up - it's called the "sniff position". This opens up the airway. You don't have to be exact and don't futz too much with the position. Sometimes opening the airway will actually allow the victim to breathe - because they still have some drive to breathe but aren't awake enough to keep their airway open.

3) If you still don't see them breathing pinch their nose closed between two fingers - you can even use this to keep them in the "sniff position", cover their mouth entirely with yours and blow air into their lungs. Everyone the first time they do this is worried they will blow too hard... that's OK. Just keep blowing and increasing the force with which you blow until you see their chest wall rise. It's a little less than the force you need to blow up a balloon. Try to give a good full breath each time. You will get faster after the first couple of breaths.

4) At this point, you will realize that this is fucking disgusting. No one who has respiratory arrest has a pretty mouth. There is often spit and snot in their mouth. It's like licking the floor of a public bathroom bad. I've done this before a number of times and each time it's insanely disgusting. However, you have to suck it up (not the spit literally). This person will probably die if you don't endure the grossness. No pressure... but seriously, you just have to. One suggestion from someone who has done this: after each breath, turn your head to the side and spit for all you are worth. Use your sleeve to get the shit off your mouth between breaths. You actually have time. You only need to give a person 12 breaths a minute to keep them safe. Each one takes a second or 2, so you have some spitting time.

5) If you are alone and help isn't coming, every few breaths scream for help again.

Note: this is what you would do for witnessed respiratory arrests - you saw the person inject the heroin and just stop breathing. If you come across someone who is down for an unknown time, you really need to do Hands Only CPR.
